Options are excluded so the figure counts only shares outstanding; on the SEC beneficial-ownership basis (options added to both numerator and denominator) it would be 8.30%. Computed, not stated in the filing.

ecosystem.notes: Bookings is a non-GAAP measure (sales of Robux and subscriptions, before deferral). Roblox records revenue gross, as principal, so Revenue includes the money later paid to developers; developer exchange fees are an expense line, defined as "the amount earned by developers and creators on the Roblox Platform that are qualified and registered in the Developer Exchange Program." Revenue / Bookings therefore overstates what Roblox keeps. Developer exchange fees are the expense recognised in 2024, not necessarily cash paid in 2024.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Roblox records revenue gross, so revenue already includes amounts later paid to developers; the share would understate what creators receive.

footprint.notes: Roblox reports DAUs, hours engaged and bookings by region (US and Canada, Europe, APAC, Rest of world), but in the FY2024 10-K and the Q4 2024 Supplemental Materials (s27.q4cdn.com, fetched) the regional values appear only inside chart images; only the year-over-year growth rates are text. Those chart values were not transcribed, because a quote must be text in the document. The one text-verifiable regional user figure is the 10-K's 'approximately 79% of our DAUs ... derived from outside the U.S. and Canada region'. The 10-K lists data centers in Florida, Georgia, Illinois, New Jersey, Texas, Virginia, California and Washington and abroad (France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, the Netherlands, India, Australia, the U.K.) without sizes, so they are not sites. Revenue by region is in the records and not repeated.
